source: ATCC reference strains and INSTAND proficiency-testing (RV) strains; no clinical/environmental source
study_type: in vitro diagnostic cross-reactivity study (EIA specificity)
evidence: "Candida tropicalis ATCC 28707, ATCC 90874, RV-7/98, RV-1/00 ... 0 0 4"; "We studied the specificity of the PLATELIA CANDIDA Ag enzyme immunoassay by using 130 isolates of 63 clinically relevant fungal species."
notes: Antigen-assay specificity study; C. tropicalis strains are reference or proficiency-testing strains of undocumented origin; no AST, genotype or source.

main_reason: Meets general rule; AST by Vitek-2 S/I/R without stated breakpoint standard or MICs
source: clinical samples: blood (20), urine (10), pus (3) C. tropicalis isolates
programme_institution: Subharti Medical College, Meerut (Western Uttar Pradesh)
evidence: "C.tropicalis 33 27.73%"; Table 1 Blood 20, Urine 10, Pus 03; Table 4 "C.tropicalis n= 30 1 2 33 0 0 28 3 2 33 0 0 33 0 0 27 2 4" (FLC S/I/R 30/1/2, VRC 33/0/0, CAS 28/3/2...)
notes: No CLSI/EUCAST document or MICs reported, so IC8 not met; included in the review but kept out of pooled estimates. Country taken from the title (hospital in Western Uttar Pradesh).

main_reason: Meets rule via IC3 (oral lesions/dentures of patients with oral candidiasis); no AST
source: oral mucosal lesions, denture fitting surface and deep denture resin of 20 elderly patients with oral candidiasis
identification_method: CHROMagar Candida + API 20C AUX (+ corn meal agar morphology)
programme_institution: Dental and Oral Medical Center, Kurume University Hospital
evidence: Table I: C. tropicalis lesions 1+1, inner fitting surface 2+1, deep denture resin 1+1 positive samples; "identification of isolated strains, the API 20C Auxanogram kit ... was used"
notes: n=7 is the count of C. tropicalis-positive samples across sites (2 lesions, 3 fitting surfaces, 2 deep resin), not necessarily distinct isolates/patients. Dentures worn by patients assigned to C1 (patient colonisation); could alternatively be considered a device. No AST.

source: 4 ATCC reference strains + 1 'clinical' strain (44) of unstated origin
programme_institution: University of New Mexico / Raymond G. Murphy VA Medical Center
evidence: "One clinical (44) and four reference (ATCC 750, ATCC 44508, ATCC 44509 and ATCC 200956) strains of C. tropicalis were studied."
notes: Only one non-reference strain and its specimen source, country and identification method are not documented (US affiliation only).

source: ICU patients: colonisation sites, blood cultures, urine
evidence: "Le diagnostic mycologique s'est déroulé en 4 étapes : prélèvement, examen direct, culture et identification." "1 souche de C. tropicalis parmi 10 testées" (FLC); "résistance ... pour 4 souches de C. tropicalis" (AMB)
notes: Congress proceedings abstract (J Mycol Med 2017). No identification method, no AST method/criterion, no MICs; AMB denominator and site breakdown of C. tropicalis unclear.

source: wet and dry sand from three recreational bathing beaches (Hobie, Fort Lauderdale, Hollywood)
programme_institution: University of Miami / South Florida beaches
evidence: "The most frequently isolated yeasts were Candida tropicalis and Rhodotorula mucilaginosa." Table 2 lists only species presence in wet/dry sand.
notes: Number of C. tropicalis isolates/positive samples not reported (only presence and pooled yeast CFU). Compartment C5 vs C6 debatable (heavily used bathing beaches, no documented discharge).

main_reason: Meets rule via IC3 (oral cavity isolates of HIV patients); virulence only, no AST
source: oral cavity of HIV-positive patients (Emílio Ribas Institute of Infectious Diseases, São Paulo)
study_type: experimental in vitro / Galleria mellonella virulence study
identification_method: HiCrome Candida + germ tube + chlamydospore + API 20C
programme_institution: UNESP São José dos Campos; Emílio Ribas Institute
evidence: "Twenty-four clinical strains of Candida spp. isolated from the human oral cavity"; "C. tropicalis (n=2)"; "isolated from the oral cavity of HIV-positive patients seen at the Emílio Ribas Institute ... (São Paulo, Brazil)"
notes: Only enzymatic activity and G. mellonella virulence; no AST or genotype. Included only under IC3.

main_reason: Case report with individual MICs for one C. tropicalis isolate
source: palatal/nasal bone tissue, chronic maxillofacial osteomyelitis (1 patient)
programme_institution: All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Jodhpur
evidence: "Candida tropicalis was grown on culture which was sensitive to Caspofungin (MIC 0.125 μg/ml) and Amphotericin B (MIC 1 μg/ml) and showed MIC >/= 256 μg/ml for fluconazole and MIC >/= 32 μg/ml for itraconazole ... by VITEK-2 automated system."
notes: n=1; IC8 met by individual MICs only. Country from patient care setting (AIIMS Jodhpur), not only affiliation.

main_reason: Candidemia isolates with CLSI M27-A3/M27-S4 MICs per isolate
source: blood cultures from ICU patients in three tertiary hospitals, Natal (RN)
identification_method: CHROMagar Candida + MALDI-TOF MS + ITS sequencing
programme_institution: Three public tertiary hospitals, Natal; UFPE / CETENE
evidence: "C. tropicalis (n=16/50, 32%)"; "testes de sensibilidade antifúngica, para todas as cepas ... de acordo com as diretrizes CLSI M27-A3 e M27-S4"; Table 4 MICs per isolate, e.g. "C. tropicalis CRN2 0,5(S) 0,25(S) 1(R)..."
notes: Text categories (1 AMB-R, 1 VRC-R, 2 FLC-SDD) disagree with the Table 4 per-isolate categories (several VRC/CAS/AFG R); use per-isolate MICs at extraction.

source: DNA extracted from unspecified clinical specimens (single centre) + standard strain BNCC 186815
programme_institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Ningbo University
evidence: "A total of 60 batches of clinical C. tropicalis DNA samples were tested."; "Clinical DNA samples ... were identified using next-generation sequencing"
